nearbyCountiesFullText.nwsHeadline: WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM MIDNIGHT TONIGHT TO 10 AM CST FRIDAY
nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
* WHAT...Lake effect snow expected. Accumulating wet snow likely away
from the lakeshore with localized snowfall totals of 3 inches or
greater possible.

* WHERE...Lake County, IN.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 10 AM CST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions, especially on bridges
and overpasses. The hazardous conditions will impact the Friday
morning commute.
nearbyCountiesFullText.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for Indiana can be obtained at https://511in.org.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

During lake effect snow, the weather can vary from bands of locally
heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.

nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
Rain in a band of lake effect showers will transition to snow
tonight, which will continue through Friday morning. Localized
slushy snow accumulations may occur wherever the band is most
persistent in portions of northwest Indiana and far northeastern
Illinois north of the Kankakee River and roughly near and east of
I-57. The Friday morning commute may be affected. Those driving
late tonight through Friday morning should allow for extra travel
time and plan for potentially slick roads and sudden sharp
visibility reductions.

discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 121734
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1234 PM EST Thu Nov 12 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Lake effect rain showers develop today with a mix of lake
  effect rain and snow showers later tonight into Friday 
  morning. Some light accumulations are possibly on grassy 
  areas, mainly west of US Route 35, with the greater potential 
  of over 1 inch accumulations closer to the Indiana/Illinois 
  stateline into far northwest Indiana. 

- Additional lake effect snow showers are possible for southwest Lower
  Michigan into far northwest Indiana late Friday night into 
  Saturday morning, but confidence in any travel impacts is low.

- Below normal temperatures today through the weekend followed
  by slowly moderating temperatures into the mid and upper 50s
  by the middle of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 235 AM EST Thu Nov 12 2026

The vigorous upper level short wave which brought the rain and 
isolated thunderstorms yesterday is departing the area across Ohio. 
Some deformation type forced precip continues across NW Ohio
early this morning with fairly tight low/mid level thermal 
packing on backside of this system. This precip should 
wane/depart to the east over the next few hours. Meanwhile, 
precip has transitioned to cellular lake effect rain showers 
across southwest Lower Michigan into northwest Indiana as cold 
air builds south behind this wave. Some respectable depth to 
lake induced instability is noted in latest GFS/RAP forecast 
soundings even this morning, but low level wet bulbs should keep
precip types primarily in the form of rain. Will be monitoring 
the next significant upper level trough across the northern 
Great Lakes as it sags southward to the southern Great Lakes 
late this afternoon into this evening. This system should allow 
for continuation of lake effect rain showers and a period of 
scattered to numerous showers associated with upper level 
vorticity advection and some weak low-mid level frontogenesis 
forcing with a reinforcing southward sinking baroclinic zone. 
Highs today will likely be reached early afternoon and then 
possibly become more steady in the mid 40s as low level cold 
advection becomes established with a good deal of cloud cover.

The secondary strong synoptic trough should clear the area by late 
this evening, but guidance has been consistent in another small 
compact vort dropping through western portion of broad negative 
upper height anomaly across the western Great Lakes overnight. 
The evolution of these successive short waves may take focus for
more dominant single banding west of the local area tonight 
into extreme northwest Indiana closer to IN/IL stateline. Little
movement in larger scale negative mid/upper height anomaly 
combined with collective warming effects from anomalously warm 
Great Lakes waters should allow the much more aggressive cold 
advection push tonight into Friday AM to affect eastern 
Wisconsin/northeast Illinois and extreme northwest Indiana. 
These type of setups sometimes tend to favor an induced weak 
northerly low level jet closer to the western shore of Lake 
Michigan which may end up being more of a focal point for 
stronger low level convergence tonight into Friday AM. NBM probs
of greater than 1" of snow tonight into Friday AM remain 
maximized west of the local area. Some uncertainty remains 
whether any one area will be affected by dominant banding for an
extending period with some potential that smaller scale 
misovorts could be embedded in any banding given good deal of 
horizontal shear across western portion of Lake Michigan. 

With focus for tonight into Friday AM looking to be shifting a bit 
farther west than previous indications, confidence remains low on 
any impacts as far east as local forecast area. Some modest drying 
in DGZ could also occur briefly in wake of the stronger secondary 
upper trough this evening with better mid level RH profiles in DGZ 
displaced to the west. Low level wet bulbs will also likely be quite 
marginal which raises questions as to what could be very low snow to 
liquid ratios, particularly if stronger banding and higher 
precip rates are west of the area. Did maintain some high 
chance/low likely PoPs tonight across far western portions of 
LaPorte/Starke Counties but it is possible these PoPs may need 
to be lowered if mesoscale trends discussed above continue to 
support more of an extreme NE IL/NW IN setup. 

Forecast confidence diminishes heading into Friday and Saturday
with continued indications that focus for daytime lake effect 
rain showers should be across extreme northwest Indiana. By 
Friday night into Saturday, trends continue to point toward 
preference to eastward migrating dominant banding with slight 
eastward progression of stagnant longwave pattern. This could 
provide another window of some lake effect snow showers to mix 
in Friday night into Saturday AM with some light accums possible
inland for grassy areas, but DGZ should begin to dry out more 
sharply during the day Saturday. Confidence in travel impacts
remains quite low for Friday night/Saturday given drying DGZ and
diminishing depth of lake induced instability.

The longwave pattern will remain relatively stable this weekend into 
first part of next week with only a slow moderation in temperatures 
back to near normal or slightly above normal. Medium range guidance 
does suggest stronger southwest flow upper level short wave lifting 
out of SW CONUS for middle of next week, but background mean upper 
ridging may be strong enough to keep bulk of precip chances NW of 
local area with this system.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 1231 PM EST Thu Nov 12 2026

Cyclonic, northwesterly flow continues this afternoon and
evening with winds sustained around 10-13 kts and gusts between
20-25 kts. Lake effect rain showers continue downwind of Lake
Michigan in NW Indiana, including at KSBN. Another wave of
showers is likely to pass through NE Indiana and NW Ohio this
evening, including at KFWA, as a trough pivots through. MVFR
ceilings prevail through the early overnight hours, with a brief
period of IFR ceilings possible at KFWA as that trough comes
through around sunset. Dry conditions return after 06Z with a
gradual, slow return to VFR ceilings possible during the day
Friday as the main lake effect band shifts west.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 7 AM EST Saturday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...Johnson

spc.text:
SPC AC 121619

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1019 AM CST Thu Nov 12 2026

   Valid 121630Z - 131200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON
   OVER A SMALL PART OF EASTERN PENNSYLVANIA AND CENTRAL NEW JERSEY....

   ...SUMMARY...
   Strong to severe thunderstorms capable of producing isolated severe
   hail, a tornado or two, and perhaps damaging winds may impact parts
   of the coastal Mid-Atlantic this afternoon.

   ...Eastern PA/NJ/Northern DE...
   Latest surface analysis shows a developing surface low over northern
   VA.  This low is expected to deepen somewhat through the day and
   track eastward across NJ as a potent shortwave trough moves into the
   region.  The zone near the surface low and extending eastward along
   the surface warm front will be a focused region of ascent and
   destabilization this afternoon, with forecast soundings showing
   MLCAPE of 500-900 J/kg, steep lapse rates, and considerable
   low-level shear/helicity profiles.  A consensus of morning
   HRRR/RRFS/REFS solutions show the development of isolated supercell
   storms in this focused area.  The risk area is quite small, but
   given the consistent guidance have opted for a small SLGT risk to
   cover the potential threats.  Hail is probably the main concern with
   any persistent supercell structure, but a tornado or two is also
   possible.  Refer to MCD #2451 for further details.

   ..Hart/Dean.. 11/12/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 121707

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1107 AM CST Thu Nov 12 2026

   Valid 131200Z - 141200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. Friday and
   Friday night.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper-level wave currently off the CA coast will progress inland
   and into the Southwest through the day Friday. A combination of
   cooling mid-level temperatures and broad ascent ahead of the wave
   will promote widespread showers and thunderstorms across southern
   AZ, NM, and into western TX through the day. Latest CAM ensemble and
   calibrated guidance suggests some wind threat could materialize
   across southern AZ/NM through the afternoon, and possibly into far
   West TX during the evening hours. However, these solutions may be
   overly influenced by recent RRFS solutions, which show more
   substantial moistening and ascent (and consequently better buoyancy)
   ahead of the upper wave compared to other guidance. Omitting these
   solutions, the general consensus is that buoyancy and shear through
   the CAPE-bearing layer will remain too limited for robust/organized
   convection. 

   Elsewhere, occasional lightning flashes appear possible along the
   northern CA and OR coasts as a secondary upper wave and attendant
   cool mid-level temperatures overspread the Pacific Northwest. This
   wave will spread east overnight and may support sporadic lightning
   flashes across the Great Basin, though lightning coverage will
   likely remain below 10%.

   ..Moore.. 11/12/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 120743

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0143 AM CST Thu Nov 12 2026

   Valid 141200Z - 151200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are forecast across the U.S. Saturday and
   Saturday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   A mid-level shortwave trough is forecast to move eastward across the
   Desert Southwest on Saturday and into the southern Plains Saturday
   night. Thunderstorms will be possible near the trough during the day
   from the Four Corners southeastward into the southern Rockies. As
   the trough moves into the southern Plains Saturday night,
   thunderstorm development will be possible across parts of west and
   central Texas. If the ECMWF solution pans out, which is much faster
   and further south, increasing low-level moisture and instability
   during the overnight period could be enough for a few strong storms
   in the Texas Hill Country. If later models runs validate the ECMWF
   solution, a Marginal may need to be considered for parts of
   west-central and central Texas, mainly for Saturday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/12/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
